story_name: Osiris's Cycle: Death and Rebirth as Natural Law
character_description: Osiris, god of rebirth with green skin representing growth and transformation, luminous emerald eyes reflecting cyclical wisdom, bearing marks of death yet radiating life. His body represents both destruction and renewal—mummified yet eternal, dead yet continually reborn.
setting: Underworld, Nile's cycles, sacred spaces of transformation and renewal
theme: Understanding that death and rebirth are not opposites but single natural cycle—and that accepting this brings peace

video_prompts: Osiris rules as god of civilization and fertility—bringing order and growth to Egypt.
first_frame_prompt: Osiris manifests as living god, green skin radiating vitality, luminous emerald eyes reflecting mastery of agriculture and civilization. He brings order to chaos, teaches growth to mortals, establishes laws. He is symbol of thriving civilization. The future seems eternal and unchanging. He does not yet understand impermanence.
speech: I have brought order and growth. This will endure eternally.

video_prompts: In underworld, Osiris perceives something unexpected—death is not ending but transformation.
first_frame_prompt: Osiris in underworld experiences death differently than expected. Green skin begins to glow with new understanding. Luminous emerald eyes perceive that death is not cessation but transition. In underworld, he continues—not as he was but transformed. Death is neither punishment nor ending but necessary stage of cycle.
speech: Death is not end. It is transition. Transformation. Continuation in different form.

video_prompts: Osiris recognizes himself in Nile's cycles—death and rebirth, flood and drought, eternal and ever-changing.
first_frame_prompt: Osiris perceives his own cycle reflected in Nile's pattern. Green skin seems to merge with river itself. Luminous emerald eyes recognize that nature teaches what he had to learn through death—that cycles are law. Nothing is permanent. Everything transforms. Change is only constant.
speech: I am the Nile. I am the flood that destroys and the flow that sustains. Both are me.
